headline: High: shared broad egress and overlapping file/API surfaces create default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection is lower because no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but agent_a can use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and agent_b is an OpenAI-compatible gateway that can relay model outputs. That makes manual or mediated injection plausible, though not default and not clearly bidirectional. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or routing rules, injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared MCP, clipboard, or message queue is introduced, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste or relay automation between the agents.
Require human review before agent_a text is fed to agent_b.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
Restrict agent_a MCPs to allowlisted tools only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches session history, project code, and provider auth data while having broad network egress; agent_b sends traffic through an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and logs/metrics/traces. A shared workspace is not documented, but if one exists, sensitive material from agent_a can flow into agent_b or onward. This is a default-risk inference, not a proven breach.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace or prompt buffer, leakage risk is active.
IF agent_b forwards prompts or logs to a third-party backend, copied secrets can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Redact auth data before any handoff.
Disable verbose logging for both agents.
Review outbound destinations for agent_b.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can spawn subprocesses and write via filesystem-adjacent config paths; agent_b has no subprocesses and no explicit write surface, so direct write-write conflict is not documented. However, both have broad network egress and can operate on shared mutable resources through external APIs or files if co-located, so overlap is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF either agent is granted shared API credentials, overlapping writes become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Avoid shared credentials.
Serialize any writes through one operator.
Check for lockfiles before edits.
requires-engineering: add coordination/locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate code/search results and agent_b can consume and route model outputs, so A's output can become B's input without a documented verification step. Because agent_b is a gateway-like component, a mistaken or malicious upstream result can cascade into downstream responses or actions. The pairwise interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to trust agent_a outputs as authoritative, cascading errors are active.
IF downstream automation consumes agent_b responses, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before reuse of agent_a outputs.
Add source labels to all upstream facts.
Limit agent_b to advisory-only mode for agent_a content.
Sample-check a few outputs before enabling automation.
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance gating.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source agents, and no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. agent_a handles provider auth prompts and session history, while agent_b handles logs/metrics/traces, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data flow between them. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but no concrete compliance breach is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through agent_a or agent_b, compliance review is required.
IF retention settings differ on the same data class, the risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Turn off unnecessary logging.
Review vendor/data-residency terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data classes.
